property_summary: A Deposit call from this test contract never reverts when sending any nonnegative amount of wei (i.e., Deposit succeeds for any value), so reverted == false for all valid calls.
If this test contract sends a positive amount of wei to C.Deposit, the call must succeed (not revert).
If this test contract has enough ETH to send amt (>0), then calling Deposit with amt does not revert (reverted == false).
When calling Deposit with any nonnegative wei amount from this test contract, the call does not revert (i.e., reverted == false).

Invariant: After any sequence where an address deposits only via Deposit/payable (including receive) and later calls Collect(x) successfully, that caller's stored balances[address] in the reference is never less than it was immediately before the Collect call (i.e., Collect only decreases the caller's balance by the collected amount); the mutant breaks this because Deposit subtracts deposits, allowing Collect to produce different balances for some addresses after completion.

For any actor A and amount d, if A deposits d then later calls Collect(x) (which sends x to A when allowed), the total balance recorded for ANY address k after Collect completes equals the prior balance plus any independent deposits (i.e., Collect only moves value out of the caller's balance by x and does not change unrelated balances) — the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can make some other key's balances differ after Collect.

For any depositor A and any amounts, after A deposits some value (via Deposit/receive) and then calls Collect(x) the reference contract preserves that A's balances[A] after Collect equals prior balances[A] - x (if Collect succeeds) and no other address's stored balances change; the mutant's incorrect Deposit (subtracting on deposit) will make some address's balances differ after Collect for some fuzzed inputs.

After depositing then depositing again, the stored balance for the sender is monotonically non-decreasing (second balance >= first balance).
After a Deposit of x by an address, that address's balance increases by exactly x compared to its prior balance.

property_summary: Calling Deposit with amount v never decreases the caller's recorded balance (balances[msg.sender]) compared to its value just before the call; it is non-decreasing and increases by at most v.

Invariant: after Deposits and a subsequent Collect by an address, the caller's balance in the reference contract is either unchanged except for the collected amount (i.e., balances[caller] == oldBalance - collected) — the mutant resets the caller's balance on Deposit causing mismatches when Deposit is used before Collect, so for some fuzzed inputs balances differ after Collect.

For any actor who has previously Deposited some ether then later Collects an allowed amount, the reference preserves that actor's remaining balances as balances[actor] == deposits - collected; the mutant that zeroes the balance on Deposit can cause balances to be lower (loss of previously stored funds) so after Collect the stored balance can differ — detect by fuzzing actor and amounts with an adversarial receiver that always accepts the transfer.

For any actor who makes a Deposit then later Collects an allowed amount, the reference preserves that actor's stored balance so that balances(actor) equals prior deposits minus collected amount after Collect; the mutant that zeroes the balance on Deposit can make balances differ for some deposits/collects.

For any depositor A and any attacker address L that rejects payment, if A has deposited funds and then Collect(...) is called (with L set as the Log file so AddMessage calls external Log), the reference C will not revert the Collect (it only calls Log.AddMessage after successful external call) and will preserve that balances for other addresses K unchanged; the mutant that zeroes balances[msg.sender] on Deposit can cause balances at some key K to differ after Collect when Log.AddMessage reverts or behaves adversarially.

For any depositor A and any recipient R used as the Log contract, if A deposits some funds (possibly via receive) and then calls Collect(amount) which succeeds sending Ether to A, the reference preserves balances of all other addresses K (i.e., balances(K) unchanged); the mutant that zeros balances[msg.sender] on Deposit can cause balances at some other key to change after Collect when the Log contract is a malicious reentrant contract that calls back into C and triggers another Deposit for the original depositor, changing balances for other keys — so the rule: successful Collect does not change balances(k) for any k != msg.sender.
After calling Deposit with value v, the caller's balances getter increases by at least v (i.e., new balance >= old balance + v).
